name: Singleton–Cosingleton Classes
definition: For each integer $n\ge4$, let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The **singleton–cosingleton class** on domain $[n]$ is $$\mathcal A_n=\{\{i\},[n]\setminus\{i\}:i\in[n]\}\subseteq2^{[n]}.$$ A subset is identified with its binary indicator function. Thus the class has all singleton supports and all complements of singleton supports, but neither the empty support nor the full support.
comments: Migrated from the survey's signed intersection-completion example. It separates projected positive recursive teaching from order compression by an unbounded ratio. The lower bound n >= 4 is part of the family definition.
